convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I've been skimming extra food. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
June shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Peyton owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Peyton said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Rest when you can. We'll talk again soon."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"I don't distrust anyone exactly — I just haven't finished trusting most of them yet. There's a difference. A slow one."
"Between us — Still on who you don't trust."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Peyton always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I do push-ups at dawn. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I asked Maren about that question — Maren's gone. Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching? Not that it matters."
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Why do you ask? Still on your read on people here."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I know you and Maren were close. I'm sorry."
"I'm picking up Maren's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"What got you through the first week? The very first days!"
"Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Between us — Honestly? I don't think anything got me through. I just didn't stop. Some mornings that's the whole story — you keep not-stopping until not-stopping feels like a plan."
"Still on what got you through the first week."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? You'd know about that."
"Maren is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sleep's gone strange. I rinse the cup twice at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"The fire feels smaller without Maren. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About that question — What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Since Maren died... I keep expecting to see Maren at the fire. Stupid."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 6 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.' No point pretending otherwise."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Jovan. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"I rinse the cup twice for Maren, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"What's this about? Still on what's been happening."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? At night I talk to someone who isn't there anymore."
Their whole posture softens around you.
"Still on their secret."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took Tashi — The Wrong Map, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration. But what do I know."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"making do. Sounds small. But small useful things stack — and one day you look up and you're the person everyone asks. That's how it happens."
"Still on the most useful thing you've learned."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "The Wrong Map. They just... took Tashi. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Ask me tomorrow. Everything changes by tomorrow."
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You said you're still figuring everyone out. Figure anything out yet? Anyone you're watching?"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
"Here. I made an extra." Hazel presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Still on that personal stuff. ...at least, that's how it looks to me."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"

"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The whole fire was arguing about Murkcap last night — what to even CALL it. 'Loud-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"Under my breath, when I'm working. Old songs from Manila, Philippines. The words are half gone but the tune holds. Tunes outlast everything."
"Still on whether you still sing."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Have you heard what they're calling Murkcap? Hazel is pushing 'Big Loud'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"Anyway." A small smile.
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Peyton Lee is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: 🕯️ Peyton Lee is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Peyton — and Peyton is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d42: That night, they bring Peyton home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d41: At the grave, June, Hazel, Torill and 3 more speak for Maren — "Peyton trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d41: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 3,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.
burialWindowSay: d41: The village's quarrel was with Peyton — and Peyton is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.

d43: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+4 integration)
d44: You say a few words for Peyton. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d44: You bury Peyton. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
d45: At the grave, Hazel, Torill, Jovan and 2 more speak for June — "Maren trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
echoSample: d44: "Peyton owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d44: "I keep turning over the last thing Peyton said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d44: "Good question." "Peyton always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."

d86: Dawn. You wake rested. (+3 health, energy restored. By the fire. Good enough.)
d86: "Here. I made an extra." Hazel presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
d86: ...and then it lands: Torill speaks 🇺🇸 English. A few shared words. Gestures. Patience.
d86: 🤝 Torill joins your party. "...Fine. This had better be worth it."
